draft.title: Using a dichotomous key
card: A dichotomous key is a tool for identifying an organism. It is a series of steps, and each step gives two choices about a feature you can observe.
At each step, pick the choice that matches the organism. Each choice sends you to another step or to a name.
Every choice splits the group in two, so the possible organisms get fewer. You stop when a choice gives a name instead of another step.
The choices must be clear features, such as has wings or has no wings. A dichotomous key only identifies an organism. It does not show how closely organisms are related.
draft.remember: A dichotomous key narrows the group with two-way choices until one name is left.

a.q: Why does each step in a dichotomous key give two choices?
opts: Each choice splits the group, so fewer organisms remain
Each choice shows how closely two organisms are related
Each choice checks the habitat and diet of the organism
Each choice lets you guess the name before you finish
a.why: Two choices split the group in two, so the possible organisms get fewer at every step until one is left. A dichotomous key only identifies organisms. It does not show how closely they are related, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the group after each choice.

b.q: Sam uses a dichotomous key to identify a beetle. Step 1 gives two choices: wings covered by a hard case, or no hard case. What should Sam do?
opts: Look at the beetle's wings and pick the matching choice
Pick the first choice, because it is listed first
Skip to the last step to find a name faster
Pick the choice with the longer description
b.why: Each step asks about a feature you can observe, so Sam must look at the beetle and pick the choice that matches. Taking the first choice without looking could send Sam to the wrong name.
b.clue: The choices describe a feature of the organism.

a.best: Each choice splits the group, so fewer organisms remain

b.best: Look at the beetle's wings and pick the matching choice
